points.description: Real internet traffic does not satisfy the assumption that packet arrivals in disjoint time intervals are independent, so the Poisson model's assumption fails.
Real internet traffic arrives in bursts rather than at a steady, memoryless rate.
The probability of a packet arrival at a node is influenced by previous arrivals at that node, so arrivals are dependent.
In on-demand video streaming, the client selectively requests the next video segments depending on its current playback state.
Because segment requests depend on playback state, network utilization is uneven over time, with low utilization likely directly after a segment has been loaded.
